sampling_model.design: For fixed-law supporting results, regular samples jointly identify \(p\), \(r\), and \(\mu\). For uniform questions, row \(n\) contains independent observations with fixed finite supports and cell-probability floors indexed by \(\kappa_n\). The zero-coverage diagnostic uses uniform \(2\times2\) response-study cells, fixed deployment margins, and Bernoulli means \(2b_n/n\), where \(b_n=1/\log(n+1)\) after finitely many rows.
sampling_model.units: Target contexts and actions are multinomial draws; separate interventional response units identify every finite \((c,x)\) cell. Dependence across stacked regular components is allowed through a declared row influence vector. In the singleton diagnostic the margins are observed without error and only the four response means are sampled.
sampling_model.treatment: The response study observes micro action \(X\); target macro action \(h\) uses an unknown context-only selector calibrated to \(r\). The response-boundary theorem changes only the sampling law and ridge for the identified micro-response means and does not alter the causal selector class or target interval.
sampling_model.overlap: The class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) imposes floors on \(p_n\), \(r_n\), and \(\pi_n\), but no lower bound on Bernoulli response means. It therefore contains the zero-coverage singleton even though deployment and study-cell probabilities are fixed. The comparative open question uses the primitive subclass \(\eta\leq\mu_{n,cx}\leq1-\eta\); whether the proposed margin and numerical-step rates suffice there is not proved.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On the singleton, the stacked estimator and empirical-influence multiplier both converge to a degenerate Gaussian law in absolute bounded-Lipschitz distance. With probability tending to one all responses are zero, every ridged cost estimate equals \(b_n/n\), the multiplier critical value is zero, and the true cost equals \(2b_n/n\). For general use, a simultaneous primitive region \(\mathcal R_n\) can instead be projected through the endpoint maps to obtain a coverage-preserving fallback.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Specified version-assignment laws identify overall multiple-version effects.
Section 2.1.1, Theorem 1, Equation (4), gives a constructive sharp identified set for partially linear coefficients from unlinked outcome and covariate margins.
Causal consistency requires intervention behavior to commute across related structural models.
Constructive causal abstractions relate low-level and high-level models through state and intervention maps.
Proposition 1 and Definition 6 give the all-intervention partial-projection condition, while Equation 11 fixes a canonical residual conditional law for a fixed low-level SCM and abstraction map.
The COTA objective is jointly convex in causally constrained transport plans.
Estimated measures and costs produce optimal-face transport limits.
Parametric optimization theory gives directional expansions of optimal values under nonunique solution and multiplier sets.
Danskin's envelope theorem expresses directional derivatives through the optimizing set.
The numerical delta method consistently estimates directionally differentiable limit laws with a slowly vanishing step.
Derivative-based resampling restores inference for directionally differentiable maps when the ordinary bootstrap fails.
The linear-program value procedure has a delta-conditioned uniform-consistency guarantee under optimizer multiplicity.
PDX precision strategies are compared with clinically meaningful controls under known recommendation rules.

For fixed \(\mu\), the selector endpoints are affine linear-program projections and shrinking positive margins alone do not violate Cho--Russell's compactness, bounded-envelope, feasibility, or fixed positive absolutely continuous perturbation requirements. Their theorem is therefore a transferred benchmark for that fixed-cost reduction. Joint estimation of \(\mu\) from cells with \(\pi_{n,cx}\geq\kappa_n\downarrow0\) is not directly covered because the inverse-cell representation need not have their uniformly bounded envelope.

For fixed \(\mu\), an epigraph formulation gives an affine projection, but Gafarov's uniform positive slack constant fails on the full shrinking-margin transport class: on a \(2\times2\) row of total mass \(\kappa_n\), the residual norm of two nonnegativity constraints is at most \(\kappa_n\), so the class slack tends to zero. His theorem also requires the stated rank, no-overidentification or dual-uniqueness, and moment conditions. Jointly estimated \(\mu\) is a transferred benchmark only on subclasses satisfying those conditions and uniform moments for the estimated coefficients.

body.tldr: The selector-specific SCM construction yields an exact causal transport image, an incremental application of standard finite coupling geometry rather than a new transport identification theorem. The new uniform result is a diagnostic for the direct Hong--Li-style paired multiplier numerical-delta implementation defined here: on one fixed-margin, fixed-cell singleton with response means \(2b_n/n\), both absolute bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian approximations vanish while its envelope has coverage tending to zero for every deterministic step schedule. This does not refute Hong and Li's theorem and is not an impossibility result: the witness has collapsing response variance, lacks any fixed response-interiority or nondegenerate-variance bound, and projecting an honest simultaneous primitive region through \(L\) and \(U\) yields an honest fallback. Comparative width and shrinking-margin rates remain open on an explicitly response-interior subclass.

project_justification.gap: Available affine-LP methods do not settle the same joint rare-margin and estimated-cost problem under the present assumptions. For fixed \(\mu\), Cho--Russell remains a transferable randomly perturbed-LP benchmark even as margins shrink, whereas Gafarov's uniform positive slack condition fails on the full shrinking-margin transport class. When \(\mu\) is estimated from response cells whose probabilities may approach zero, neither transfer is automatic because inverse-cell influence envelopes or moments can diverge. The procedure-specific numerical-delta rate and width comparison therefore remains open after imposing response interiority.
project_justification.niche: The incremental contribution is a schedule-independent zero-coverage response-boundary diagnostic for the direct Hong--Li-style paired empirical-influence multiplier numerical-delta implementation defined here, together with an exact projected-region fallback. It is not presented as a counterexample to Hong and Li's theorem. The next subfield question is comparative: on a common response-regular subclass, does row-feasible numerical delta buy narrower intervals or weaker margin-rate requirements than projection or transferred affine-LP methods? The conjectured \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold is not an established frontier.
project_justification.fill: The note sets \(b_n=1/\log(n+1)\) after a finite-row adjustment, uses Bernoulli means \(2b_n/n\), and proves that the all-zero event tends to probability one, collapses the empirical-influence multiplier critical value to zero, and forces coverage to zero although both absolute bounded-Lipschitz discrepancies vanish. It also defines \(\mathrm{CI}_n^{\mathrm{proj}}=[\inf_{\widetilde\beta\in\mathcal R_n}L(\widetilde\beta),\sup_{\widetilde\beta\in\mathcal R_n}U(\widetilde\beta)]\) and proves the deterministic inclusion from primitive-region coverage. The remaining comparison is confined to \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}\).

body.related_work: VanderWeele and Hernán motivate specified version-assignment laws, and Béal and Latouche supply the PDX setting. D'Haultfoeuille, Gaillac, and Maurel derive a distinct constructive sharp set from unlinked margins in a partially linear data-combination model; the finite transportation image here is standard coupling geometry, and its paper-specific content is attainment inside the displayed selector-specific SCM family. Rubenstein et al. and Beckers--Halpern supply general commutation and abstraction semantics. Xia--Bareinboim Proposition 1 and Definition 6 supply the exact all-intervention partial-projection condition instantiated selector by selector here; this note does not extend their general abstraction theorem and does not preserve one fixed Equation-11 canonical Layer-3 map. Hundrieser et al. analyze empirical optimal transport with estimated costs and optimal-face limits, while Danskin and Bonnans--Shapiro supply the underlying envelope and parametric-LP sensitivity machinery; the fixed-law endpoint derivative here is therefore a finite transportation specialization rather than a distinct sensitivity theorem. Fang--Santos and Hong--Li supply derivative-based and numerical-delta inference. The zero-coverage theorem targets only the direct paired empirical-influence multiplier implementation of the Hong--Li numerical-delta recipe defined here under the displayed absolute bounded-Lipschitz approximations; it neither asserts that Hong--Li's theorem covers the collapsing-variance triangular array nor refutes that theorem. Voronin supplies delta-conditioned uniform consistency for an LP-value procedure under his conditions; it does not by itself provide the paired simultaneous confidence envelope here or verify this response-boundary array. With fixed \(\mu\), each endpoint is an affine transportation-LP projection. Shrinking positive margins alone do not violate Cho--Russell's compact-polyhedron, bounded-envelope, feasibility, i.i.d., or fixed positive absolutely continuous perturbation requirements, so their randomly perturbed LP is a transferred fixed-cost benchmark; it covers the identified set conservatively and attains exact coverage on an outer perturbed set, not the same interval target. Their theorem does not directly verify jointly estimated \(\mu\) with rare cells, because inverse cell probabilities can violate its common bounded envelope. Gafarov's affine epigraph formulation is another fixed-cost benchmark and permits flat primal faces, but his uniform class requires positive rank and slack constants and, in the stated main case, no overidentification and unique dual solutions. On a \(2\times2\) transport row of mass \(\kappa_n\), two nonnegativity residuals have norm at most \(\kappa_n\), so the required uniform slack constant fails as \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\); nonunique dual faces create a separate exclusion. Jointly estimated \(\mu\) transfers only after verifying an affine coefficient representation and uniform \(2+\epsilon\) moments, which \(\pi_{n,cx}\geq\kappa_n\downarrow0\) does not supply. These are benchmarks on admissible subclasses, not results for the full class here. The projected-region fallback is uniformly honest whenever its primitive region is, but no comparative width theorem is claimed.
body.interpretation: For a fixed interior deployment law, the paired numerical-delta method remains pointwise valid even with nonunique transport faces. Uniform use near a response boundary is different: absolute Gaussian accuracy can coexist with a nearly certain all-zero sample, a zero critical value, and zero coverage. Practitioners should either verify a response-interior or equally strong variance diagnostic before using that numerical-delta envelope, or use the projected-region fallback. For the Béal--Latouche PDX application, superiority to control should be reported as uniform only when the lower selector endpoint exceeds the control benchmark and the uncertainty method covers that lower endpoint; the new diagnostic warns that rare positive outcomes can invalidate the numerical-delta certificate even when allocation margins are well behaved.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The selector seed \(S\) is atomless even though all endogenous and response domains are finite. The residual coordinate is endogenous with equation \(Z_s=g_s(C,S)\), which is essential for interventions on \(C\) to commute; its induced conditional law varies with \(s\). The result proves the Xia--Bareinboim Definition-6 partial-projection identity selector by selector and does not preserve one fixed canonical Equation-11 residual law or one common canonical Layer-3 map across distinct selectors.
body.honest_scope: The paper proves a schedule-independent zero-coverage theorem for one collapsing-response singleton and the direct Hong--Li-style paired empirical-influence multiplier numerical-delta envelope defined here. The witness has response means and primitive variances tending to zero; it supplies neither a fixed nondegeneracy lower bound nor a perturbation-stable failure class, so it does not establish failure on the response-interior subclass and does not refute Hong and Li's theorem. The paper also proves an exact deterministic projection fallback from any simultaneous primitive confidence region. It does not prove a minimax impossibility for other methods, a sufficient or sharp \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold, or a width advantage over projected-region, Cho--Russell, or Gafarov procedures. Cho--Russell transfers cleanly only to the audited fixed-cost LP subclass unless additional estimated-cost envelope conditions are verified; Gafarov additionally requires uniform rank, slack, uniqueness, and moment conditions that exclude parts of the shrinking-margin and nonunique-dual class. The remaining comparison is open on \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}\). The structural SCM realization, sharp selector interval, fixed-map obstruction, fixed-interior derivative, and pointwise numerical-delta result retain their supporting scope. No effective-support cycle/equality criterion or endpoint flow-certificate theorem is claimed in this note.
